signal: A callable body contains more authored code lines than the configured maximum.
why_it_matters: A large body can conceal multiple responsibilities, make control flow harder to verify, and increase the cost of focused testing.
review: NON-NEGOTIABLE RESEARCH: Perform an external research/tool call to {reference_url} and read the page before reviewing this finding or proposing or applying remediation. If the URL cannot be consulted, report the reference research as incomplete and stop. Inspect the callable's control-flow regions, state changes, error paths, responsibility boundaries, and focused tests before deciding whether extraction is appropriate.
remediation: Separate coherent control-flow or responsibility regions into named functions or a focused module, preserving behavior with characterization tests before moving code.

signal: A callable declares more signature inputs than the configured maximum.
why_it_matters: Many inputs can make call sites difficult to understand and can indicate a missing domain value or mixed responsibilities.
review: NON-NEGOTIABLE RESEARCH: Perform an external research/tool call to {reference_url} and read the page before reviewing this finding or proposing or applying remediation. If the URL cannot be consulted, report the reference research as incomplete and stop. Inspect recurring parameter groups, independent optional modes, call-site readability, and whether the arguments form one meaningful value.
remediation: Introduce a cohesive parameter object or nominal domain value for arguments that belong together, or split independent operations instead of merely hiding unrelated parameters.

signal: A struct or enum variant declares more direct fields than the configured maximum.
why_it_matters: A large state surface can increase invalid-state combinations and can indicate that several concepts have been combined.
review: NON-NEGOTIABLE RESEARCH: Perform an external research/tool call to {reference_url} and read the page before reviewing this finding or proposing or applying remediation. If the URL cannot be consulted, report the reference research as incomplete and stop. Inspect field cohesion, invariants, construction paths, groups that change together, and whether splitting state would preserve behavior.
remediation: Extract cohesive field groups and their invariants into focused value or state types; keep the original shape when it is intentionally a flat transport record.

signal: An enum declares more variants than the configured maximum.
why_it_matters: A broad variant set can spread case knowledge across the codebase and make state transitions difficult to evolve.
review: NON-NEGOTIABLE RESEARCH: Perform an external research/tool call to {reference_url} and read the page before reviewing this finding or proposing or applying remediation. If the URL cannot be consulted, report the reference research as incomplete and stop. Inspect variant families, transition rules, repeated matching sites, and whether the enum still represents one closed concept.
remediation: Centralize variant-specific behavior and partition the enum only when the variants form independent concepts with separate change reasons.

signal: A local type owns more authored associated functions than the configured maximum.
why_it_matters: A wide behavior surface can indicate that one type owns multiple responsibilities and increases navigation cost.
review: NON-NEGOTIABLE RESEARCH: Perform an external research/tool call to {reference_url} and read the page before reviewing this finding or proposing or applying remediation. If the URL cannot be consulted, report the reference research as incomplete and stop. Inspect method clusters, shared state usage, public versus internal behavior, and natural responsibility or module seams.
remediation: Move a cohesive method cluster and the state it owns into a focused type or module, keeping a small intentional interface at the seam.

signal: The summed authored body lines of a local type exceed the configured maximum.
why_it_matters: A large aggregate implementation can hide a concentration of behavior even when no individual method is oversized.
review: NON-NEGOTIABLE RESEARCH: Perform an external research/tool call to {reference_url} and read the page before reviewing this finding or proposing or applying remediation. If the URL cannot be consulted, report the reference research as incomplete and stop. Inspect which method groups use which fields, responsibility clusters, extension points, and tests covering the type's distinct behaviors.
remediation: Separate the largest cohesive behavior clusters behind focused interfaces and add tests at those interfaces before relocating implementation.

signal: A trait declares more associated functions than the configured maximum.
why_it_matters: A broad trait raises implementation cost and can force consumers to depend on capabilities they do not need.
review: NON-NEGOTIABLE RESEARCH: Perform an external research/tool call to {reference_url} and read the page before reviewing this finding or proposing or applying remediation. Inspect implementor needs, caller subsets, required versus default methods, and whether smaller capability traits would be coherent.
remediation: Split independent capability groups into smaller role traits, using composition or extension traits when callers do not require the full surface.

signal: A field or parameter population meets the configured raw-primitive count and share.

remediation: Replace domain-significant raw values with validated nominal newtypes or value objects and convert at transport boundaries.

signal: The same named and typed slot group appears in at least the configured number of declarations.
why_it_matters: Values that repeatedly travel together may represent one missing concept and can cause parallel edits when the group changes.

remediation: Introduce a named parameter or value type for the group when its members share meaning, validation, and lifecycle; update the supporting declarations together.

signal: Different local owners have similar method bodies but different source-level interfaces.
why_it_matters: Equivalent behavior behind divergent interfaces can increase adapter code and prevent common substitution, but coincidental algorithms are possible.

signal: Several optional fields are directly used by no more than the configured share of receiver methods.

signal: A type has enough fields and no more than the configured number of non-accessor authored operations.

signal: A type meets the configured method count and syntactic delegation share.
